hints.title: Exhaustive Permutation Search
hints.text: With only four digits, there are exactly 24 permutations. Check each permutation for 24-hour clock validity.

hints.title: Time Bound Validation
hints.text: A permutation (h1, h2, m1, m2) represents a valid time if hours = h1 * 10 + h2 < 24 and minutes = m1 * 10 + m2 < 60.

hints.title: Maximize Total Minutes
hints.text: Iterate over all permutations of the four digits. Convert each valid time into total minutes = hours * 60 + minutes. Keep track of the permutation that maximizes total minutes. Return formatted as HH:MM or empty string if none valid.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy single-digit placement easily traps on edge cases like [2, 0, 6, 6] where choosing 2 first leaves invalid minutes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Since there are only 4! = 24 permutations, evaluating every permutation takes negligible constant time and memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that 4 digits is trivial to brute-force rather than writing complex greedy backtracking rules.
complexity.notes: Leading zeros in hour and minute formatting are required.
